title: Chat: decision buttons for the run's waiting options
brief:
Desktop app (React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind, folder desktop/). When a run needs the owner, the backend puts this object on the live run state (the state returned by `useClutchState()` / `clutchStore.getSnapshot()` from desktop/src/services/clutchState.ts): `waiting: { kind: 'approval' | 'escalation' | 'question', question: string, options: string[], taskId?: string } | null` and `status === 'awaiting_human'`. Today the UI only shows fixed Approve/Reject/Retry buttons, but the backend's options are e.g. ['approve','reject'] for a plan, ['accept','retry','reassign','skip','abort'] for an escalation, ['answer'] for a question.

1. Create desktop/src/components/GateOptionsBar.tsx exporting `GateOptionsBar` (no required props). It reads the state with `useClutchState()`; the `waiting` field is not in the ClutchState type, so read it with a narrow cast, e.g. `(state as unknown as { waiting?: Waiting | null }).waiting`. Render nothing unless status is 'awaiting_human' and waiting has options and waiting.kind is not 'question'. Otherwise render a compact bar: the kind as a small label, the question text (pre-wrap, max 6 lines, scrollable), an optional note <input placeholder='Note for the team (optional)'>, and one button per option (label capitalized; 'abort' and 'reject' styled as destructive, the first option styled as primary). Clicking sends `clutchStore.send({ action: 'human_decision', decision: option, instructions: note || undefined })` and disables the buttons until the status changes. Export also a pure helper `gateButtons(options: string[]): { id: string; label: string; tone: 'primary' | 'danger' | 'neutral' }[]`.
2. Create desktop/src/components/GateOptionsBar.test.tsx (vitest, test only `gateButtons`: labels capitalized, first option primary, abort/reject danger, others neutral).
3. In desktop/src/components/ChatFeed.tsx render `<GateOptionsBar />` once, directly above the chat input area (find where the input bar / composer is rendered; a single import + a single JSX line). Do not change anything else in ChatFeed.tsx.

title: Workflows: read-only graph view for looping workflows
brief:
Desktop app (React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind + @xyflow/react already installed, folder desktop/). The Workflows screen (desktop/src/components/WorkflowOrchestration.tsx) loads workflows as `CompilerWorkflow` (type in desktop/src/services/workflowFormat.ts: nodes with id/type/position/data, edges with source/target and optional data.when). Our workflows contain loops (retry/reassign edges), so the existing editable canvas refuses them and only the JSON view is shown with a yellow 'Complex workflow: please edit in JSON mode' warning.

1. Create desktop/src/components/SmurfGraphView.tsx exporting `SmurfGraphView({ workflow }: { workflow: CompilerWorkflow })`: a READ-ONLY @xyflow/react graph (import { ReactFlow, Background, Controls, MarkerType } from '@xyflow/react' and its css 'import "@xyflow/react/dist/style.css"' only if the project does not already import it elsewhere - check with a search). Nodes: use workflow node positions (if a node has no position, lay nodes out left-to-right by breadth-first order from 'start', 250px apart horizontally and 120px vertically per row). Node label: data.instruction if present else id, with a smaller second line showing data.agent (the node type, e.g. 'senior.plan'). Colour by type: start = gray, human_gate = amber, check = emerald, agent_task = blue (light Tailwind-like hex colours). Edges: arrow markers; label = data.when when present; loop/back edges (target appears earlier in the BFS order than the source) drawn as type 'smoothstep' with a dashed style. fitView, nodesDraggable=false, nodesConnectable=false, elementsSelectable=false. Height 520px, full width, rounded border.
   Export also a pure helper `layoutOrder(workflow: CompilerWorkflow): string[]` returning the BFS order of node ids from 'start'.
2. Create desktop/src/components/SmurfGraphView.test.tsx (vitest) testing only `layoutOrder` (start first, BFS order, unreachable nodes appended at the end).
3. In WorkflowOrchestration.tsx: where the 'Canvas' tab is shown for a workflow that is not canvas-compatible (search for the incompatibility handling / the 'Complex workflow' warning or `isCanvasCompatible`), show `<SmurfGraphView workflow={...} />` instead of disabling the Canvas tab, so clicking Canvas shows the graph. Keep the JSON tab working. Make the smallest change possible in this file.

title: Models panel: header overlap and benchmark labels
brief: In desktop/src/components/SmurfModelsPanel.tsx (rendered inside a settings modal that has its own close X button in the top-right corner): 1) the first section header's Refresh button sits in the top-right corner and overlaps the modal's close button - give the panel top padding (about pt-10) or move that Refresh button so nothing sits in the top-right 48x48 px; 2) in the Benchmarks list the run id (e.g. '2026-10-21-06-44') is rendered in a narrow column and gets cut to '2026-10-' - show it fully (no truncation; whitespace-nowrap and enough width) or drop it since the date is already shown; 3) in the Models section, show the adapter name in the group header in a friendlier form: 'openhands' -> 'OpenHands (ACP)', others capitalized. Only change this file.
